dlg.dez_format.title: The .dez file format
dlg.dez_format.p1: A .dez file is plain UTF-8 JSON. It contains the parts (with their position in each view), wires and traces, notes, design rules — and a "library" section that embeds the full definition of every part used.
dlg.dez_format.p2: That makes a project completely self-contained: send it by email, chat, AirDrop or USB stick and it opens in any designElectronics app, offline, with no server and no extra downloads.
dlg.dez_format.p3: Custom parts can be shared on their own as .dezpart files (File ▸ Import Part). See docs/FILE_FORMAT.md for the full specification.

up.mobile_body: Uploading to a real board needs the desktop app (macOS, Windows or Linux) with Arduino IDE 2 or arduino-cli installed.
up.mobile_body2: You can export the sketch (.ino) and open it in the Arduino IDE.
up.install_help:
To upload, designElectronics uses arduino-cli, the tool behind the Arduino IDE. Install either one:

• Arduino IDE 2 (it includes arduino-cli), or
• arduino-cli on its own: macOS  brew install arduino-cli · Windows  winget install ArduinoSA.CLI · Linux  see the install page

Then open this window again. You can also export the sketch and open it in the Arduino IDE.

part.resistor.desc: A resistor limits current. Edit the resistance in the Inspector; the color bands update automatically.
part.led.desc: Light-emitting diode. The longer leg (anode, +) goes to the positive side; always use a series resistor.
part.capacitor_ceramic.desc: Non-polarized capacitor, typically 10pF–1µF. Used for decoupling and filtering.
part.capacitor_electrolytic.desc: Polarized capacitor for larger values. The stripe marks the negative (−) leg.
part.diode.desc: Lets current flow from anode to cathode only. The band marks the cathode.
part.inductor.desc: Coil that stores energy in a magnetic field.
part.crystal.desc: Quartz crystal resonator for precise clocks.
part.potentiometer.desc: Variable resistor with a wiper. Set the wiper position (0–100%) in the Inspector; it's live in simulation.
part.photocell.desc: Light-dependent resistor: ~1kΩ in bright light, ~1MΩ in the dark. Adjust the light level in the Inspector.
part.pushbutton.desc: Momentary tactile switch. Legs on the same side of the gap are always connected; pressing connects the two sides. In simulation, hold it with the pointer.
part.switch.desc: Single-pole double-throw switch. The middle pin is common. Toggle the position in the Inspector or click it while simulating.
part.battery.desc: DC voltage source. Choose the style and set any voltage in the Inspector.
part.regulator.desc: Linear regulator (TO-220, IN-GND-OUT). Needs ~2V of headroom above the output voltage.
part.transistor.desc: Bipolar junction transistor (TO-92, pinout E-B-C). A small base current switches a larger collector current.
part.mosfet.desc: Logic-level power MOSFET (TO-220, G-D-S). Drives motors and LED strips from a microcontroller pin.
part.timer555.desc: The classic NE555 timer for oscillators, delays and PWM. Datasheet: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ne555.pdf Fully simulated: build an astable circuit and watch the LED blink.
part.ic_dip.desc: Generic dual-inline IC. Set the pin count, chip label and comma-separated pin names in the Inspector — a quick way to create any chip.
part.buzzer.desc: Beeps when powered. Longer leg is +.
part.dc_motor.desc: Small brushed DC motor. Drive it through a transistor or MOSFET, never straight from a microcontroller pin.
part.arduino_uno.desc: ATmega328P microcontroller board, 5 V logic. In simulation it is USB-powered: 5V and 3.3V pins supply the circuit, and the pins listed under "Pin outputs" are driven (e.g. D13=HIGH, D9=LOW, D5=BLINK:500, D6=PWM:30). Firmware itself is not executed.
part.breadboard.desc: HUST EIC lab breadboard: four SYB-120 style 700-point tiles on one green carrier plate. On a tile the channel separates two 5-row fields — each column of 5 holes is one net (a–e below the channel, f–j above) and the two fields are not joined. Each long edge has a segmented power row of ten 5-hole blocks laid out 3-4-3: blocks 1-3 (pins 1-15), 4-7 (16-35) and 8-10 (36-50) are three separate nets. Pin ids start with the tile number: 1j1-4j60, 1a1-4a60, top row 1u1-4u50, bottom row 1l1-4l50.
part.header_male.desc: Single-row 0.1" header for connecting modules, sensors and jumper wires.
part.header_female.desc: Single-row 0.1" header for connecting modules, sensors and jumper wires.
part.connector.desc: Generic connector: 1 row(s) of 8 pins, 2.54 mm pitch, numbered Sequential.
part.ground.desc: Schematic ground symbol. All ground symbols are connected to each other (net "GND").
part.power_label.desc: Schematic power symbol. Symbols with the same net name (e.g. 5V) are connected.
part.net_label.desc: Connects schematic wires by name instead of drawing a wire.
part.pcb_board.desc: Printed circuit board outline. Set the size in millimetres in the Inspector.

part.hole.desc: Non-plated hole for screws and standoffs.

part.rpi3.title: Raspberry Pi 3 Model B / B+
part.rpi3.desc: Quad-core Cortex-A53 single-board computer with the standard 40-pin GPIO header, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. In simulation the Pi is powered: its 5V and 3V3 pins supply the circuit and the GPIO pins listed under "Pin outputs" are driven at 3.3 V (e.g. GPIO17=HIGH, GPIO18=PWM:30, GPIO27=BLINK:500). Your Python/C program itself is not run. GPIO pins are 3.3 V only — never connect 5 V to them.
